subject: Embeddings endpoint: sudden p95/p99 jump after catalog sync - urgent
messages:
From: Sara Martinez <sara@atlasdata.co>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-04T08:15:20-08:00
Subject: Embeddings API severe latency spike since catalog update

Hi Jordan / Redwood support,

We're seeing a sudden increase in embeddings latency starting ~07:50 PST this morning after you applied the catalog sync. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s and p99 is near 3.8s. Our batch ingestion jobs are timing out and downstream similarity searches are returning stale results.

Sample request ids: rq_8f3a2b, rq_8f3a9d (attached). We're running the hosted embeddings endpoint in us-west with the standard model alias. No config change on our side.

Can someone confirm whether the catalog push rolled a new quantization profile or model variant? We need ETA to resolution — this is affecting production ingest.

Thanks,
Sara Martinez
Director of Data Platform, AtlasData

Attachments: p95_p99_timeseries_20261204.png; sample_requests_20261204.txt

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Martinez <sara@atlasdata.co>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-04T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings API severe latency spike since catalog update

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm escalating to infra and the catalog team (Ben, Marissa). We just kicked a catalog sync across hosted regions at 07:45 PST (tag: catalog-sync-2026-12-04-3).

Ben / Marissa: can you confirm whether that rollout included any model variant changes (quantization profile, kernel selection) that could impact tail latency? Also please surface any mitigations we can apply immediately (rollback, pinning AtlasData to previous model, throttled routing).

I'll keep Sara updated with ETA and will open an incident in parallel.

-Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-04T09:12:30-08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings API severe latency spike since catalog update

On Fri, Dec 4, 2026 at 8:40 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben / Marissa: can you confirm whether that rollout included any model variant changes (quantization profile, kernel selection) that could impact tail latency?

Short answer: yes — the sync included a staged rollout of a new kernel selection heuristic that prefers int8 kernels for the xformer-embed-1 family in us-west for cost savings. We saw positive perf on our canary (smaller sequences) but not enough long-tail testing.

Initial findings from infra: KV cache hit behavior changed slightly for long prefix sequences which can push some requests onto a slower slow-path for attention recompute. We're reproducing locally with the Atlas sample requests and seeing p99 spikes consistent with their numbers.

Mitigations I can trigger immediately:
- Roll back the kernel heuristic (full rollback of catalog-sync-2026-12-04-3) — impact: 10–15m to rollback across region.
- Pin AtlasData account to previous model variant (no global rollback) — impact: near-immediate but requires routing override for account id.
- Enable conservative batching and disable the new kernel for long sequences (partial config change) — impact: might reduce throughput, less risky than full rollback.

I'll start pinning AtlasData if we get sign-off. Need a business decision on rollback vs account pin.

-Ben
Engineering Lead, Model Catalog

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-04T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings API severe latency spike since catalog update

Ben thanks — good triage. Neha, can you stand up a quick patch to pin AtlasData routing to the prior model variant and enable a conservative fallback for long-prefix requests? Ben, if pinning is quick, do that first while we prepare the rollback plan.

Jordan / Sara: proposed immediate steps:
1) Pin AtlasData to previous model variant (low risk, near-immediate) — action: Ben/Neha
2) Rollback catalog-sync-2026-12-04-3 if pinning doesn't normalize p99 within 30 minutes — action: Ben
3) Offer AtlasData a one-time credit for the ingestion disruption and hold a postmortem with timeline within 48 hours — action: Jordan (customer comms)

Sara, can you confirm whether you want us to proceed with pinning now?

-Marissa
Senior PM, Hosted API

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Executive summary: AtlasData embeddings latency incident

Executive summary for leadership / finance:
- Incident: Hosted embeddings p95/p99 spike for AtlasData after model catalog sync (catalog-sync-2026-12-04-3).
- Timeline: 07:45 PST catalog rollout; 07:50 PST customer observed p95~1.2s / p99~3.8s; 08:40 internal escalation; 08:55 pinning applied; 09:10 p99 partially reduced to ~1.1s; full rollback queued as contingency.
- Impact: AtlasData ingestion jobs delayed, customer engineering team blocked for ~2 hours; potential revenue impact on their weekly pipeline run.
- Actions taken: routing pin for AtlasData (Neha), monitoring throttling enabled, incident opened INC-2026-1124, postmortem scheduled.
- Recommended exec asks: approve up to $8k in one-time credits for AtlasData and sign-off on a cross-team postmortem to prevent kernel heuristic rolls without extended long-sequence canaries.

Ben / Marissa / Neha — attach the logs and the mitigation runbook to the incident link above. Jordan — please confirm customer-facing credit offer and schedule for the postmortem.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Go-to-Market Operations
